chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Kufi, who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a boy who plays with a girl whom he does not own and has not reached puberty, is it permissible for his father to buy her and have intercourse with her? He said: The forbidden act does not make the permissible forbidden, so this report does not contradict the reports we have previously mentioned, because his saying 'plays with a girl' may be a metaphor for non-intercourse; as for with intercourse, then she becomes forbidden to him in all cases, according to what we have previously mentioned.

key_terms.لَا يُحَرِّمُ الْحَرَامُ الْحَلَالَ: The forbidden does not make the permissible forbidden

ai.seo_question: Does a father's marriage to a girl become forbidden if his son has intercourse with her first?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the phrase 'playing' (yab'ath) is ambiguous and may refer to non-intercourse acts, thereby not prohibiting the father from marrying the girl; however, if actual intercourse (jima') has occurred, she becomes permanently forbidden to him. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'the forbidden does not make the permissible permissible' (la yuharrimu al-haramu al-halala), distinguishing between minor sexual contact and full consummation in determining marital prohibitions.
